overview.title: The same components, two different orders
overview.explanation: The ownership chain shown is first, where Prefix owns Limit and Limit owns Plain. The second chain reverses the wrapper order. Triangles describe type substitutability; ownership arrows describe who destroys which object. Calls travel inward and results return outward.

focus.title: Add a prefix to the inner result
focus.start: // Ask inward before adding our text.
focus.what: Prefix transforms the complete text returned by its inner component.
focus.where: This block executes after the inner text call returns.
focus.why: One prefix operation can wrap plain or already-decorated text.
focus.invariant: The inner object exists and is called once for this result.
focus.risk: Moving this behavior inside a limiter changes which text is cut.
explain: The comment identifies inward delegation before transformation.

focus.title: Limit the inner result
focus.what: Limit takes a prefix of whatever its inner component returns.
focus.where: This block is the length policy at its chosen position in the chain.
focus.why: The same wrapper can limit raw text or the result of another feature.
focus.invariant: Zero yields empty text; an oversized limit keeps the full body.
focus.risk: A byte substring can split multibyte text if the ASCII assumption is removed.
explain: The comment defines the scope of the length rule.
